Subject: POC planning - Lakeside Health (success criteria & RACI)

Hi Sara / Mark —

Thanks again for taking the time this morning. Quick recap and proposed plan so we have alignment before the formal MOU/POC kickoff: 

Summary of the call:
- Goal: Validate Redwood Inference for clinical notes summarization and search workflows in Lakeside’s pilot clinics.
- Pilot scope: 3 clinic sites, up to ~50k notes processed over a 4-week evaluation window.

Proposed success criteria (please confirm or modify):
1) Accuracy: F1 >= 0.78 on the validation set you provided (clinical summarization).
2) Latency: 95th percentile generation time < 1.2s per request under expected load (see throughput assumptions in shared sheet).
3) Integration: End-to-end export of summarized notes to your EHR test environment without data loss for 95% of records.
4) Cost & ops: Per-record inference cost within the threshold you approved during discovery (TBD in MOU).

Evaluation plan & timeline:
- Week 0 (now–June 11): Finalize success criteria, security checklist, and network/infra owners.
- Week 1 (wk of June 14): Deploy POC in Lakeside test VPC (private deployment); ingest sample dataset.
- Weeks 2–5 (June 21–July 18): Run evaluation, collect metrics and qualitative feedback.
- Week 6 (by July 25): Review results and decide go/no-go.

Ownership / RACI (proposed):
- Infra (network, VPC, provisioning): Lakeside owner — Mark Rivera (owns VPC, peering, firewall rules).
- App integration (EHR export, API integration): Lakeside app team — Sara Thompson (integration owner), Redwood SE — Aditya Rao (technical lead).
- Security & compliance: Redwood security lead — Rishi Malhotra (point for checklist & SOC2 evidence). Lakeside security reviewer — TBD.
- Procurement / contracting: Lakeside procurement (procurement@lakesidehealth.com) — commercial and SOW signoff.
- Project management / success criteria sign-off: Sara + Redwood PM (Lauren Bishop).

Action items / next steps:
- Sara: confirm infra owner (Mark) and procurement contact (listed above).
- Mark: confirm network constraints and any required IP allowlists.
- Lakeside: confirm success criteria or propose edits by EOD Thursday (June 3).
- Redwood: we’ll attach the success criteria workbook and network requirements doc for your network team.

Attachments: POC_Success_Criteria.xlsx (workbook with metrics & test plan), Network_Requirements.pdf (network / allowlist guidance).

If that looks good I’ll schedule the kickoff for week of June 14 and share a short mutual action plan doc.

Thanks —
Marissa

Thanks Marissa — solid recap. A few quick confirmations and tweaks: 

- Confirmed success criteria: the accuracy target looks right; I’ll validate on our side and confirm any adjustment by Thursday.
- Timeline: the week of June 14 works for our infra team, but can we aim to complete deployment verification (connectivity + sample ingest) by June 16 instead of June 18 if Redwood availability allows? That would help our clinical team start earlier.
- Infra owner: confirmed — Mark Rivera will own VPC peering & firewall rules. Mark (cc’d) will loop in our network ops and confirm IP ranges.
- Procurement: procurement@lakesidehealth.com is the right address for the SOW. They typically need ~7–10 business days for standard SOW review.

Two asks for Redwood before kickoff: 
1) Please share SOC 2 Type II summary / or a statement where we can access it (our security team will need this).
2) The Network_Requirements.pdf — our network team will review; if you can include sample allowlist entries and port ranges that will speed routing approvals.

If Redwood can confirm deployment availability on June 14 and provide SOC2 evidence + allowlist examples by EOD Friday (June 4), we’ll lock the kickoff calendar.

Best,
Sara

On 2026-05-30 10:05, Sara Thompson wrote:
> Thanks Marissa — solid recap. A few quick confirmations and tweaks:
> ...

Sara / team — quick security notes from our side: 
- SOC2: we’ll provide a SOC 2 Type II summary link and a non-confidential evidence bundle for your reviewers by EOD Friday. I’ll also send the internal controls mapping to typical HITRUST controls if that helps.
- Data handling: For the POC we recommend tokenization + ephemeral KV cache only (no persistent full-text storage by default). If Lakeside requires persistent retention in your VPC, we’ll document retention options and redaction patterns.
- Encryption & KMS: Redwood supports customer-managed keys (via KMS/HSM) for Private deployments. Please let us know if Lakeside has a preferred KMS provider (AWS KMS / Azure Key Vault / On-prem HSM).
- Minimum network requirements: we’ll add a one-page summary to Network_Requirements.pdf emphasizing outbound allowlist and mutual TLS endpoints.

I’ll take the lead on the security checklist and be the Redwood point for technical security review.

-Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Security Lead, Redwood Inference
